messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Customer-OrionSystems | ap-southeast1 dedicated pool | p99 latency spike above SLO (90m window). Pager triggered for on-call. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/3690012345 :rotating_light:

ena-oncall: I'm on it. seeing p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.8s for their tenant -traffic stream. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/tenant/orion/ap-southeast1

raj-sre: grabbing logs and live traces. Any recent deploys for that pool?

lina-runtime: No deploys in last 6 hours. We have higher small-model traffic for that tenant (embedding-heavy). Could be KV cache pressure.

oliver-infra: infra metrics look OK for node health, but host CPU on pool nodes creeping 75-85% during spike. Disk i/o normal. Not seeing autoscaler activity matching burst.

ena-oncall: Quick mitigation checklist: 1) throttle tenant to reduce QPS 2) enable traffic split to fallback hosted variant 3) add burst nodes to dedicated pool 4) prefix cache warmup. I'll start 1 and 2.

lina-runtime: +1. How to trigger fallback? We can flip routing policy to route new requests for tenant-orion to model variant 'orion-fallback-v1' hosted in us-east temporarily. Command: ``/runbook route-change tenant=orion variant=orion-fallback-v1 region=ap-southeast1 mode=graceful``

ena-oncall: running step 1: applying soft throttle to tenant via quota override. Command: ``redwood admin qoverride --tenant orion --qps 45 --duration 15m``

ops-bot: ACTION: quota override created by ena-oncall for tenant=orion qps=45 expires=15m id=qo-98765

raj-sre: still seeing p99 ~1.6-1.9s on traces. Throttle reduced throughput but tail latency unchanged on in-flight KV misses. Need to inspect cache hit rates.

lina-runtime: cache hit rate for that tenant dropped from 92% to 48% at the time window. KV cache eviction pressure spikes when they hit longer prompts + embeddings. We'll attempt targeted cache prefill for top prefixes.

oliver-infra: initiating burst: provisioning 4 extra GPU nodes into ap-southeast1 dedicated pool (burst capacity commit). This is a warm-add; should take ~3-5m. Command: ``infra add-burst --pool orion-dedicated --count 4``

ops-bot: TASK: infra.add-burst job started by oliver-infra id=burst-4421 status=provisioning

maya-customer-success: I'm on a call with their SRE team. They're reporting increased 502s on their side when p99 spikes. Also asking for mitigation ETA. I'll tell them soft throttle + fallback is in progress; provisioning burst nodes now.

aaron-se: FYI their traffic pattern shows an hourly batch that aligns with their ETL window, sharp tail latencies caused by long-context embedding lookups. We recommended smaller batch sizes in earlier onboarding but they haven't applied it.

ena-oncall: flipping routing to fallback now (graceful). If that works, we can keep a proportion of requests on dedicated pool and send non-critical or large-context requests to hosted fallback. Running: ``/runbook route-change tenant=orion variant=orion-fallback-v1 rate=40%``

ops-bot: ROUTE_CHANGE: staged routing change by ena-oncall tenant=orion variant=orion-fallback-v1 rate=40% stage=1/3

lina-runtime: After switching 40% traffic, p95 drops to ~200-260ms, p99 still at ~1.1s. That's progress. Need to warm KV cache on remaining 60% of dedicated requests. I will run cache-prefill for top 100 prefixes we saw in last 24h.

raj-sre: logs pulled for a sample slow request: ``trace_id=tx-9234: model-run time breakdown: queuing 120ms, decode 210ms, kv-miss-fetch 650ms, network 30ms``. kv-miss-fetch dominating.

lina-runtime: Prefill runnable: ``redwood cache prefill --tenant orion --prefix-file top100.txt --pool orion-dedicated``. Kicking it off, tracking progress.

oliver-infra: burst nodes are up (status=ready). Autoscaler didn't trigger due to conservative signal; we should revisit heuristics later. For now nodes live.

ena-oncall: With burst + 40% fallback + prefill: p95 ~220ms, p99 ~450-700ms. We can keep incremental routing at 30-50% until traffic subsides or they change batch size.

maya-customer-success: Customer asks: will they be billed for burst? I'll confirm billing policy but recommend we cover emergency burst for now and discuss later.

aaron-se: agree on covering as a one-time emergency credit; suggest we add a follow-up to recommend changing batching, or moving heavy embedding jobs to off-peak or dedicated smaller model.

ena-oncall: rolling handoff to raj-sre for sustain/monitoring for next 2 hours. I'll update incident doc and jump to customer call. raj: you have lead.

raj-sre: taking lead. Checklist I'm doing now: 1) verify p99 under SLO for 15m window 2) keep routing at current 40% fallback 3) monitor KV hit rate, prefill progress 4) gather traces for postmortem and recommend config changes.

ops-bot: HANDOFF: ena-oncall -> raj-sre at ts=3690012398

lina-runtime: prefill completed 78/100 prefixes. Observed 13% immediate increase in hit rate; more prefixes queued. Prefill script logs attached: ```
[INFO] starting prefill
[...]
[INFO] completed 78 prefixes, eta 1m
```

raj-sre: p99 now holding ~420ms for last 5m, p95 ~210ms. Marking incident 'mitigated' status monitored. I'll keep an eye; if we regress we'll escalate back to ena and infra.

maya-customer-success: told customer we have sustained improvements, offered to coordinate their engineering changes (batch size reduction) and to schedule a mitigation runbook review next week. They appreciated that. :thumbsup:

oliver-infra: note to self: autoscaler thresholds too conservative for sudden KV-heavy workloads. Filing infra ticket: INFRA-1294 to revisit scaling signal and warm pool behaviors.

ena-oncall: creating incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/3690012345/postmortem. Will add timeline and RCA after further investigation.

ops-bot: INCIDENT: status=mitigated by raj-sre mitigation_summary="throttle + routing fallback + burst nodes + kv prefill"

raj-sre: Actions/next steps for postmortem: - confirm root cause: cache eviction under high long-context embedding workload - propose runtime change: adaptive prefetch + per-tenant cache quotas - infra change: loosen autoscaler or add predictive warm pool - customer action: reduce batch size or schedule heavy jobs off-peak - billing: CS to confirm emergency burst credit

maya-customer-success: I'll own customer follow-up and billing conversation. I'll also schedule a runbook walkthrough with their SRE team.

lina-runtime: I'll prototype an adaptive prefetch PoC and add telemetry to detect cache-thrashing tenants.

oliver-infra: I'll update autoscaler ticket and include suggestions from runtime about signals we can use.

ena-oncall: thanks all. Closing active paging. Raj keep monitoring for 1 hour then handback to standard on-call.

raj-sre: Will monitor. If no regressions by 1h, will close thread and mark for postmortem writeup.

ops-bot: NOTE: thread will be archived after incident status closed for 7 days.
